doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Lessons with Mr. Baroni
summary: He started lessons at about thirteen, working on Bach, Beethoven and Hanon scales with a teacher who wanted him reading well by sixteen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So before you could form a band you had to get proficient on your instrument, so when you first started playing piano and you started taking lessons-again could you name that gentleman? Was that your first piano teacher?
And how old were you when you first started taking piano lessons?
Yeah, well, in between thirteen and fifteen. Somewhere in there, I’d say thirteen.
And what types of lessons? Was he just working on scales, technique, what books did he have you working out of?

We had Bach and Beethoven book, so I mean . . . I learned how to read that music and that’s basically what-we had a book of scales, that was very prominent, a lot of piano players tried it out, Hanon, you know books like that and it was good, he was very good. He wanted to see me at sixteen being able to read the music and being able to articulate what was on the page and I thought it was very good. From there I formed my R&B band and eventually a jazz band.
